role: commenter, Allan Hancock College area resident
summary: William Denneen, writing from the Allan Hancock College area, draws on 12 years of personal ORV ownership and local observation to argue that ORVs have been very destructive to natural habitats. He cites noise disturbance to wildlife and people, vegetation damage from tires, and littering as specific harms. He calls for severe restrictions on ORV use and an outright prohibition in wildlife refuges.

statement.text:
Allan Hancock College 500 South College Drive Sinta Maria, California 93454
July 13, 1972
Director
Bureau of Outdoor Recreation
Department of the Interior
Washington, D.C. 20240
Dear Director,
Re: INT-DES-72-62
I wish to add my observations to your consideration of offroad-vehicle plans on public lands. We have a considerable number of such vehicles in our area and I have owned one for 12 years.
My observation has been that ORV's have been very destructive to the natural habitat in all areas where they are permitted. The noise disturbs wildlife and people, the tires tear up vegetation and the drivers often leave prodigious quantities of litter. ORV's should be severely restricted and prohibited in wildlife refuges.
Sincerely yours,
Villiam Denneen
